sol.problem:
A nonzero Born branch is silently assigned zero probability and cannot be selected. Reproduced a memoryless ptr_width=32 object with action a signature {"abi":"0.8","args":[],"bounds":[],"in":[],"kind":"action","mem":[],"mut":[1],"tier":"q"}, body:
action @a (t:wire mut) () () () ()
^entry():
rx 1e-200 t
and cc p signature {"abi":"0.8","kind":"cc","params":["qreg[1]"],"results":["i1"],"tier":"cc"}, body:
fn cc @p (q:qreg[1]) (r:i1) () () ()
^entry():
action_call @a (q) () () ()
r = measure q
ret r
After hash substitution, check succeeds (object_hash 2b04b6368b47532aeb80fd1e4f8204b0d4f3a969e9cc6ddd30bb2318c72e60d6). run-action a --mut 1 prints exact support {"0":[0,-5e-201],"1":[1,0]}. Hand: Rx(theta)|1> = -i sin(theta/2)|0> + cos(theta/2)|1>; theta is a nonzero finite dyadic, so P(0)=sin²(theta/2)>0, approximately 2.5e-401. Under the existing ascending-outcome/CDF draw convention, draw=0 lies in the first nonempty outcome interval and must select 0. Actual run-cc p --arg qreg:1 --draws 0 completes in 3 steps with measurement/result 1. measurement_branches computes norm2 in f64, underflows to 0 and scales that branch by infinity; measure skips it. Boundary controls: 1e-100 and 1e-161 with draw=0 select 0; 1e-162 and 1e-200 select 1; zero angle selects 1; draw=0.5 selects 1 throughout. No execution budget is needed for this three-row CC trace.
sol.fix: Change src/quantum.rs::measurement_branches and src/registers.rs::measure (with exact.rs support if needed). §14.2 requires "projective computational-basis measurement with Born probabilities" and §4.4 defines rx(theta)=exp(-i theta X/2); neither permits deleting a nonzero outcome. Keep exact support authoritative and use probability magnitudes/CDF comparisons and projection normalization that cannot underflow a positive branch to semantic zero: extended-exponent or rigorously refined probabilities are possible; binary64 display probabilities may remain approximations. Do not merely clamp to a guessed probability. Add the exact fixture above to tests/cli_xam.rs: --arg qreg:1 --draws 0 must complete in 3 steps with r=0, measurement bits "0", no fault; draw=0.5 must give r=1; replacing angle with 0.0 must give r=1 at draw=0. Add tests/quantum.rs/registers.rs coverage for the same tiny branch with an unmeasured register and a subsequent measurement, asserting a finite, usable conditional state and the correct Born result. Reversal of a measured run must remain refused (§10).

sol.section: §5.6 translation lemma, §9.2 program points, §12.1 structural claims; src/claims.rs::Object::check_translation_witness
sol.problem:
The implemented structural checker never reads witness.frame and never checks that the named circuit is V;W;V^-1;W. Reproduced memoryless ptr_width=32 perm_action a, signature mut=[1], in=[1], mem=[], args=[], bounds=[], body:
perm_action @a (t:wire mut) (p:wire in) () () ()
^entry():
b = qborrow any 1
cx p b
cx b t
cx p b
cx b t
qreturn b
Its interface/closure hash H is c59dfefb9f3d8e91d5a3ba0bd74e37dc0ff4fcf7b73069ad4d9bd4760224672a. In an otherwise valid bound certificate, put one claim {"kind":"structural","rule":"translation_lemma","subclaims":[],"witness":{"V":[[H,"entry",1]],"W":[[H,"entry",2]],"X":["p"],"B":["b"],"frame":[[H,"entry",1],[H,"entry",2]]}} and leave verification.borrow_frames empty to exercise the claim checker itself. check exits 0/status ok (object_hash c548c42057e64ea1fd635c14743ad0196457081057daa58efdb961bfefc72115). A temporary read-only-library harness calling Object::parse and verify_certificate returns Ok([ClaimReport {region:"a",index:0,kind:"structural",verdict:Proof}]). But the explicitly named two-gate frame maps (b,t,p) to (b XOR p,t XOR b XOR p,p): it neither restores b nor removes t's dependence on b. The full four-gate frame is valid and run-action a --mut 0 --in 1 returns t=1,p=1; that does not prove the different truncated frame. check_translation_witness only checks the separately listed V/W gates' side conditions. Independent re-execution in check_borrow_independence limits the effect on borrow_frames admission; it does not make this false ClaimVerdict::Proof correct.
sol.fix: Change src/claims.rs::check_translation_witness and the program-point resolution it uses, optionally rejecting bad endpoints earlier in certificate.rs::validate_claim. §5.6 says "the frame is V; W; V^-1; W" and frames are "maximal contiguous permutation-only subcircuits"; §12.1 requires "check the rule's side conditions syntactically against the object and the subclaims' results". Resolve both frame endpoints and all V/W points using §9.2 ordinals "counting nested lines in text order"; verify actual borrowed wires, the complete named frame, exact reverse V and repeated W, with no omitted intervening gates or non-permutation boundary. Only then return Proof. Add a tests/r1_certificates.rs test constructing the bound certificate with the usual certificate helper/template: the exact truncated [entry:1,entry:2] claim must make verify_claim/verify_certificate return a §5.6/§12.1 error; the complete [entry:1,entry:4] witness must return Proof. Also reject nonexistent/reversed endpoints and a changed second W; include a nested-line ordinal positive so .instructions.get(ordinal) cannot substitute for the canonical resolver. No target, schedule, numerical or channel machinery is involved; this is the already-implemented structural path.

sol.section: §5.1 signature order, §9.4 region ABI, §12.1 expected program; src/claims.rs::Object::verify_claim_guarded/execute_element
sol.problem:
Expected-program comparison binds inputs by the subject's local names instead of the shared signature positions. Reproduced memoryless ptr_width=32 functions with identical perm_action signatures mut=[1], in=[1], mem=[], args=[], bounds=[]:
perm_action @a (t:wire mut) (p:wire in) () () ()
^entry():
x t
x t
perm_action @id (u:wire mut) (v:wire in) () () ()
^entry():
x u
x u
Both are the identity on their two-bit interfaces. Their closure hashes are a=e153e6770967051bba7f7f3fb4f3a1ebc24ac36acf625fb577316a72fefc3b89 and id=44e334e5b7c16cf020004825850687841b6f2aad00bfc0774452b0cb9a575d72. Add a valid certificate region record for a with claim {"kind":"exhaustive","label":"proof","domain":{"bundles":[{"name":"t","width":1,"lo":0,"hi":1},{"name":"p","width":1,"lo":0,"hi":1}],"borrowed":[],"regions":[]},"expected":{"program":"44e334e5b7c16cf020004825850687841b6f2aad00bfc0774452b0cb9a575d72"}}. check succeeds (object_hash 066383fd91d1388dc39bc6af32af8a2cbec3a2e95ba02c8d0ee71370016fce58); run-action a --mut 0 --in 1 and run-action id with the same options both produce state {"01":[1,0]}. Hand enumeration: 00,01,10,11 must compare equal. Actual verify_certificate, invoked through the frozen library, returns Err("§12.1: claim 0 of e153...: element 1 differs from the expected program"). verify_claim_guarded passes unchanged Component::Bundle("t"/"p") elements to execute_element(id,...); its value("u"/"v") lookup silently defaults both to zero, so it compares [0,1] to [0,0].
sol.fix: Change src/claims.rs::verify_claim_guarded and the input representation used by execute_element. §12.1 requires "re-execute every domain element on the reference interpreter / expected program; compare full tuples"; §9.4 says interface bundles/regions are "passed in declared order", and the recorded SPEC-QUESTIONS 21 reading specifies the final tuple "in signature order". Map subject interface components to the expected program by interface group and position (and region cell index), independently of local parameter names; retain borrowed pool components in their domain order. Preserve deliberate zero initialization for genuinely omitted partial-domain inputs, but never treat a renamed corresponding parameter as omitted. Add the exact four-element identity-vs-renamed-identity claim to tests/r1_certificates.rs; verify_claim and verify_certificate must return Proof. Add a region-name-renaming equivalent and a negative reference performing a single X, which must still fail on a full-tuple mismatch. This corrects the implemented exhaustive checker and needs none of staged deliverables 8-11.

codex.fix: Change src/borrow.rs::Compiler::compile and the Node/Evaluation Repeat representation to retain the start and end of every borrowed lifetime and prove its required factorisation before each return; iteration-local borrowed variables must not be treated as one continuously live borrowed system across iterations. §4.3 defines qreturn as "matched inverse of qborrow after its frame"; §5.1 requires "every qborrow by a qreturn after its frame"; §5.6 requires "P_F = P′ ⊗ I_B"; §4.6 specifies "body n times". Expected: the exact object and its unrolled form both fail Object::parse and hash/check (exit 1, empty stdout, §5.6). Add these negatives to tests/r1_borrow.rs and the differential generator. Positive controls: (a) move qborrow before the loop and qreturn after it, keeping one X per iteration; (b) keep borrowing inside but put two X gates before each return. Both must parse and run/reverse unchanged for t,b=0/1 and a borrowed wire entangled with an untouched reference. Include nested-loop forms so an outer even repetition cannot mask an invalid inner return. Do not reject all loop-local borrowing or require each iteration to restore a borrowed bundle whose lifetime actually spans the loop.

codex.problem:
Dynamic aliases of region operands produce an internal error instead of the specified CC trap/fault record. Reproduced memoryless ptr_width=32 signatures a={"abi":"0.8","args":[],"bounds":[],"in":[1],"kind":"action","mem":[],"mut":[1],"tier":"q"}, p={"abi":"0.8","kind":"cc","params":["i1","qreg[1]","qreg[1]"],"results":[],"tier":"cc"}, bodies:
action @a (t:wire mut) (s:wire in) () () ()
^entry():
cx s t
fn cc @p (c:i1, q:qreg[1], r:qreg[1]) () () () ()
^entry():
s = select c q r
action_call @a (q) (s) () ()
ret
Rehashed check returns status ok. run-cc /dev/stdin p --arg 1 --arg qreg:0 --arg qreg:1 exits 1, empty stdout, stderr "§3.3: action interface bundles overlap". run-program and reverse fail identically. Hand: select makes s the same handle as q; the second instruction fails the disjoint-interface precondition and must record FAULT_UB_TRAP without changing wires. region_record deduplicates the ids before complete_call can detect this overlap; action_internal later returns an unmarked Error, propagated by step. With c=0 the same program completes in 3 steps and reverse equals_entry=true. Also reproduced a control-target version: child a has only mutable t with x t; parent uses the same select followed by ctl s action_call @a (q) () () (). c=1 instead exits 1 with "§3.3: effective control aliases target"; c=0 completes and reverses.
codex.fix: In src/classical.rs::region_record (or a dedicated runtime binding validator called by step), validate physical wire disjointness for all interface slots before handle-id deduplication, and validate effective-control/actual-target disjointness. Route failures of these runtime call preconditions through trap(...) so step pushes the ordinary terminal fault frame. Keep deduplication for lifecycle bookkeeping and allow legitimate overlap of a control with a read-only input where §3.3 permits it; do not indiscriminately map simulator/internal errors to traps. §3.3 states "an instruction whose precondition fails is a CC trap", "A region’s interface bundles and regions are pairwise disjoint", and every effective control must be "distinct from every target"; §4.7 binds CC slots bit for bit; §7.4 makes a fault record terminal and "reversed like any prefix". Add the exact dynamic-select witnesses to tests/registers.rs and tests/cli_xam.rs: c=1 yields CLI exit 0, JSON status FAILED, fault 4, steps 2, results [], unchanged q/r; reverse returns equals_entry=true after the faulted prefix. c=0 stays COMPLETED at 3 steps with target 1 and full reversal. Also cover equivalent R entry bindings and an oracle input/output alias.

muse.section: section 5.6, section 4.6, section 14.2; src/borrow.rs::Compiler::compile (qloop arm, lines 363-390) and src/borrow.rs::Evaluation::apply Node::Repeat (lines 694-735)
muse.problem: Borrowed wires produced inside a plain qloop body are composed as ONE carried wire instead of as fresh borrowed bundles per iteration, so an even trip count falsely proves factorisation. Witness (memoryless, signature kind=perm_action, mut=[1], in=[], mem=[], args=[], bounds=[2]): perm_action @a (t:wire mut) () () () () / regs {  } bounds {2} / ^entry(): / qloop 2 { d = qborrow any 1; cx d t; qreturn d }. After rehashing with the hash command, check exits 0 with status ok (object f349e389...), and run-action --mut 0/1 returns t unchanged only because the executor's default borrow pool is |0>. Hand derivation: iteration i borrows a fresh bundle d_i in an unknown state and applies t ^= d_i, so the operation is t ^= d_0 XOR d_1 with d_0,d_1 independent (choose d_0=1,d_1=0: t flips; with d_i entangled with external references, t becomes correlated with both) - not U_t tensor I on any borrowed bundle. The identical circuit unrolled (two distinct qborrow/cx/qreturn groups) is correctly rejected at hash with 'section 5.6: borrow frame output v0_0 depends on borrowed entry values', as is the single group and the qloop-while form of the same body (which materialises iterations and freshens wires); qloop 4 and nested qloop 2x2 with the same body are also wrongly accepted, and so is 'cx t d' once per iteration over qloop 2 (borrowed bit restored only by cross-iteration aliasing in the proof). Cause: the qborrow arm emits no Node (borrow.rs:312-320), the qloop arm wraps the once-compiled body in Node::Repeat(2,[Flip(d,t)]), and Evaluation::apply for Repeat interns one entry variable for d and squares that body map (borrow.rs:700-730), modelling d as persistent state; a qalloc in the same position is sound only because Node::Alloc resets the wire. Validation therefore depends on loop wrapping, the same soundness class as SOL-R3-B03 but for borrow lifetimes.
muse.fix: (a) Change src/borrow.rs::Compiler::compile qloop arm and Evaluation::apply/Node::Repeat handling (and Compiler::produce bookkeeping as needed): track the borrowed wires produced while compiling the loop body (including through inlined perm_action children); a body that produces borrowed wires must not be composed by repeated squaring over those wires' single entry variables. (b) Spec: section 5.6 'A region's completed operation equals its declared operation tensor identity on EVERY borrowed bundle' and 'Borrowed wires (set B) are touched ... only inside borrow frames' whose 'realised permutation P_F ... MUST factor as P_F = P' tensor I_B'; section 4.6 'qloop n { body } = body n times'; each execution of the body performs a new qborrow matched by its qreturn (section 5.1 explicit cleanup), so each iteration's frame must factor for its own fresh bundle. (c) Exact expected behaviour: the witness above (and the qloop 4, nested 2x2, and 'cx t d' variants) is rejected at load citing section 5.6 - Object::parse Err and CLI hash/check exit 1 with empty stdout - with no borrow_frames claim in the object; sound implementations either materialise iterations with fresh generation wires like the existing while arm (borrow.rs:365-375) or prove per-iteration factorisation once for body-local borrows (fresh universally-quantified borrowed inputs, outputs equal to those inputs and no influence on carried wires) and then compose only the carried-wire map by squaring; an iteration cap is not acceptable. (d) Test to add in tests/r1_borrow.rs (fails now because check exits 0, passes after): the exact witness plus its unrolled equivalent, both requiring section 5.6 rejection through parser and CLI hash/check; positives that must remain accepted and execute with exact forward/adjoint restoration on every t and every borrowed entry state: (i) borrow outside the loop (d=qborrow; qloop 2 { cx d t }; qreturn d) - one bundle, CX twice; (ii) per-iteration identity body at qloop 2 and at qloop 1099511627776 (d=qborrow; cx d t; cx d t; qreturn d) proving no unrolling/cap was introduced; (iii) extend the generated families in tests/r1_fuzz_discipline.rs with borrows born and returned inside qloop bodies, decided by an independent per-iteration freshness oracle.
